comparison: Perfect agreement on SMRT-seq methylation profiling data (C33-C41, C46-C48). Both evaluations find the methylation landscape characterization across three strains to be well-supported with solid experimental approaches and appropriate quantification methods.

Strong agreement on comparative genomic analysis and conservation patterns (C51-C54, C57-C59). Both evaluations accept the functional enrichment analysis and conservation findings. Peer review also covers C60-C61 which OpenEval addresses separately in R20.

Strong agreement on motif identification (C62-C70). Both evaluations confirm the HsdMSR motif discovery and analysis methods are sound. Peer review also includes C71-C72 (similarity to P. aeruginosa) which OpenEval addresses in R4.

Strong agreement on HsdMSR validation experiments (C73-C77, C85). Both evaluations confirm the growth curve, dot blot, mutant analysis, and complementation data demonstrate HsdMSR's role in methylation. OpenEval includes C71-C72 in this result while peer review includes them in R3.

Perfect agreement on growth phase-dependent methylation (C79-C80, C82-C84, C144). Both evaluations accept the dot blot assays and MTase overexpression experiments as solid evidence for dynamic methylation patterns.

Perfect agreement on RNA-seq analysis and differential gene expression (C86-C95). Both evaluations confirm the transcriptional profiling data are robust with appropriate statistical thresholds and functional enrichment analysis.
Perfect agreement on virulence and T3SS regulation (C96-C101). Both evaluations confirm the plant infection assays and gene expression data demonstrate HsdMSR's role in pathogenicity regulation.
Perfect agreement on biofilm formation and alginate biosynthesis (C103-C105). Both evaluations accept the RT-qPCR and crystal violet assay data showing HsdMSR's role in biofilm regulation.

Perfect agreement on ribosomal gene regulation and translation efficiency (C108-C114). Both evaluations confirm the RT-qPCR and Ribo-seq data demonstrate HsdMSR's impact on translation and metabolism.

Perfect agreement on direct transcriptional regulation mechanism (C115-C120, C140). Both evaluations accept the lux-reporter experiments with systematic mutations as strong evidence for methylation-dependent transcriptional control.

Strong agreement on MTase distribution and strain-specific methylation patterns (C121-C126). Both evaluations accept the integration of REBASE predictions with experimental data. OpenEval also includes C31-C32, C81 which peer review does not explicitly address separately.

Both address mechanistic interpretations and overall conclusions. OpenEval evaluates C107, C133 as supported mechanistic connections between growth defects and ribosomal changes. Peer review R12 evaluates C133, C143 as part of the overall study's novel insights and well-supported conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates the mechanistic model for direct vs. indirect regulation (C136-C143) as supported. Peer review R12 includes C143 in their overall assessment that the study provides novel insights with mostly well-supported conclusions.

OpenEval rates C42-C43 (6mA enrichment in intergenic regions and transcription regulation inference) as UNCERTAIN, noting the functional inference is speculative without direct testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates C127-C129 (synthesis of motif methylation data with growth phase dynamics) as SUPPORTED. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found, though related claims are covered in other peer results.
OpenEval rates C146-C147 (TF-binding site speculation) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable hypotheses requiring experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
